paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking perturbations by tag. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart, titled “The effect of context masking perturbations by tag,” illustrates the mean effect (y-axis, labeled “effect,” scaled linearly from 0 to 20) of context masking perturbations for six different multilingual BERT models (mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, XLM-B₂, each represented by a distinct color) across four distinct linguistic tags: “case,” “gender,” “number,” and “tense” (x-axis, arranged left to right). Each bar is accompanied by vertical error bars indicating the standard deviation. For the “case” tag, the effect values are highest, with mBERT-B₂ (red, ~11.5) and XLM-B₂ (red, ~11.0) showing the largest positive effects, followed by mBERT-L₂ (light blue, ~6.0) and XLM-L₂ (dark blue, ~5.5), while mBERT-R₂ (light green, ~2.5) and XLM-R₂ (dark green, ~2.0) show smaller positive effects. For the “gender” tag, all models show smaller effects, with mBERT-B₂ (pink, ~4.0) and XLM-B₂ (red, ~3.5) showing the largest positive effects, and mBERT-L₂ (light blue, ~1.0) and XLM-L₂ (dark blue, ~0.5) showing the smallest. For the “number” and “tense” tags, all models show very small or near-zero effects, with mBERT-B₂ (pink, ~2.0) and XLM-B₂ (red, ~2.0) showing the largest positive effects for “number,” and mBERT-B₂ (pink, ~0.5) and XLM-B₂ (red, ~0.5) showing the largest for “tense,” while mBERT-L₂ (light blue, ~0.5) and XLM-L₂ (dark blue, ~0.5) show the smallest for “tense.” The bars are not sorted and are presented in the order of the tags on the x-axis, with no visual emphasis on any particular bar.
